memory_update.text: UAMY should remain in the speculative/underfollowed lane because the DLA IDIQ plus DPA award is unusually material relative to company scale, but future inclusion depends on delivery-order conversion, margin, and dilution checks.

LEU is a high-relevance mid-cap government-backed capacity name tied to DOE HALEU production; next layers should distinguish funded production revenue from non-finalized or subject-to-appropriations awards.

For government-backed capacity expansion, the highest-quality signals are funded delivery orders, exercised options, finalized task orders, cost-share disbursements, and offtake/price-floor mechanics rather than announced ceiling values.

The next search pass should map subtier public suppliers beneath BWXT, MP Materials, and UAMY, especially testing/certification, specialty metals, regulated components, feedstock logistics, and qualification bottlenecks.

node: Government-backed capacity expansion: grants, IDIQs, offtakes, and loan guarantees
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around funded government demand rather than headline policy rhetoric. The strongest underfollowed leads are companies where a government-backed contract, offtake, price floor, DPA grant, or DOE/DLA award is material to existing revenue or future capacity. Priority screening should separate headline contract ceilings from actual delivery orders, funded task orders, cost-plus revenue recognition, working-capital needs, dilution, and technical execution risk.
